claims.text: The target material is equiatomic bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The target material may contain up to 1 wt.% oxygen and a realistic defect microstructure.
The proposed model is trained on conductivity data from both pristine and defect-containing HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
The proposed model uses physics-informed features representing electron-defect and electron-disorder scattering.
Point defects and oxygen interstitials act as additional electron-scattering centers in HfNbTaTiZr.
Analytical perfect-crystal conductivity formulas neglect temperature-dependent resistivity contributions from realistic defects and chemical disorder.
Embedding physics-derived scattering terms will allow the ML model to capture those neglected temperature-dependent resistivity contributions.
The ML model can predict electrical conductivity over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K with at least 50% lower error than current analytical defect-free approaches.
The model will achieve conductivity RMSE of at most 10% across the two specified temperature regimes.
Analytical defect-free models typically have conductivity RMSE of approximately 20–30%.
Analytical conductivity models for perfect HfNbTaTiZr crystals have reported errors of approximately 20% at low temperature.
Analytical conductivity models for perfect HfNbTaTiZr crystals have reported errors of approximately 30% at high temperature.
The claimed applicability is limited to equiatomic bulk polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr containing no more than 1 wt.% oxygen.
The claimed validated temperature ranges are 5–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The model is not validated below 5 K, above 1200 K, or for oxygen contents above 1 wt.%.
Prediction accuracy in the 200–300 K crossover region and for extrapolation above 1 wt.% oxygen is uncertain.
An RMSE exceeding 10% in either tested temperature regime would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis, conditions, and experiment claim coverage beginning at 0 K, while the boundary states validity begins at 5 K and explicitly excludes T<5 K. Thus the proposed test includes a temperature interval outside the stated applicability domain.
